content.text:
<user>
Return the next passage of fiction.

I go to bed when I am done reading. The next morning I wash, dress, and get breakfast in time for the scheduled orientation.
</user>

summary: **Adding character dialogue and setting orientation scene**

item.text:
You mark the chapter, carry the blue volume upstairs, and leave the common room as the card players begin collecting coins and disputed property.

In your room, silent lightning moves beyond the window. The old framed letter hangs above the desk, its promised visit still unrealized after all these years. You set the Council book beneath the lamp and go to bed.

A tower bell wakes Garvey House in the grey light before sunrise. You wash at the basin, dress in a clean shirt and your mended charcoal coat, and settle the Garvey signet onto your hand.

Breakfast is less ceremonial than dinner. Bread, eggs, porridge, fruit, and several kinds of meat wait on the sideboard. Ysolde’s portion rests on a chilled stone slab. An orientation notice has been placed at every seat.

Ashara and Rashid enter from the quadrangle carrying practice blades. Both have dust on their boots.

“Eight,” Ashara says.

“Seven,” Rashid replies.

“The last shoulder strike landed.”

“After the bell.”

“It still landed.”

Rashid takes a cup of coffee. “Then tomorrow I’ll continue hitting you after time is called.”

“That would require hitting me before it.”

He gives her a look over the rim of his cup. Ashara helps herself to four eggs.

You get breakfast with time to spare. Around you, the rest of the household gathers: Aldric returns from dawn prayer, Caelindra appears with immaculate hair and an apple in hand, and Thessaly reads the entire orientation notice down to the printer’s mark. Seraphel sits beside her with a cup of tea and acknowledges you with a small nod.

The notice directs first-year Conclave students to the eastern seminar room. Shortly before the appointed bell, the household crosses the quadrangle in a loose group.

Morning light picks out the Academy’s mismatched construction: black demon stone beside angelic marble, living branches worked into elven walls, and low arches scarred by dragon tools. Students stream toward the different colleges while the storm turns below the plateau.

The Conclave seminar room contains fifteen chairs around an oval table. Framed copies of the Accords cover the walls in seven scripts.

One person is already seated whom you did not meet at dinner. She has luminous red skin, sharply pointed ears, small dark horns, and no tail. Her name card reads:

**LYSARA VANE — EXCEPTIONAL OBSERVER**

She gives the entering group a brief salute with her pencil.

At the front of the room, an elderly angel scholar arranges folders beside the Academy seal. When the final bell sounds, he looks around the table.

“Good morning. I’m Chancellor Mordecai Ashworth. The next hour concerns schedules, faculty, Council observation, travel permissions, and the rules students otherwise insist no one told them.” He opens the first folder. “Grand principles can wait until you know which doors require whose signature.”
